industry.ipm: Indian pharma market (IPM): +13.5% in Q1FY27 (IQVIA, as quoted by Lupin and Cipla) and +11.1% on MAT Jun-26 (IQVIA via Kotak Neo); Pharmarack: Aug-2026 +10.7%, CY2026 forecast raised to 11.3%. Chronic therapies grow faster than acute (Lupin chronic +21.5% vs IPM chronic +16.8% in Q1FY27). Lupin is No.8 in the IPM (IQVIA MAT Jun-26): No.1 in anti-TB, No.2 in respiratory, No.3 in cardiac and anti-diabetes (ICRA, company).
industry.usGenerics: US generics: low-single-digit price erosion on the base portfolio (Lupin: 'mid single digit price decline due to additional competition in select products' in Q1FY27). Profits come from products few can copy - inhalers, long-acting injectables, peptides, biosimilars, first-to-file patent challenges - and last only until rivals arrive. Lupin is No.3 in US generics by prescriptions (~5.0% of generic TRx), No.1 in 56 products and top-3 in 112 (IQVIA, quarter to Jun-26).
industry.europe: Europe: budget pressure (Germany doubling some rebates) but biosimilar substitution incentives rising (France); ophthalmology biosimilars in Germany outside AOK tenders. Lupin's European sales passed USD200mn in FY26 and grew 83% in Q1FY27 with VISUfarma.
industry.emergingMarkets: Emerging markets: Brazil (+117% in local currency in Q1FY27 on dapagliflozin and empagliflozin), South Africa (Pharma Dynamics, No.7 generic company), Philippines (Multicare, 56.28%), Mexico (Grin). Semaglutide launches in South Africa (FY27) and Brazil (filing FY27).
industry.api: API: Rs969 cr (4% of sales) in FY26, down 18% as more output went captive; global leader in cephalosporins and anti-TB APIs; Dabhasa and Vizag API sites moved into Lupin Manufacturing Solutions (ICRA).
industry.fx: Rupee: Rs88.47/US$ used for FY26 (company); ~Rs93.9 implied by Q1FY27 US sales (Rs3,434.8 cr / USD366mn); Rs95.81 on 30-Sep-2026 (PTI, as recorded in our Zydus file).

brokers.thesis: Another beat, but FY27 is a consolidation year: Tolvaptan and Mirabegron competition offsets new launches, earnings flat over FY26-28; limited upside
US dips to ~USD250mn a quarter but recovers to USD300mn+ in FY28 on launches; industry-high margins, 50 US and 80 India launches, complex generics doubling
Broad-based beat; management's FY28 US growth guidance is optimistic vs the street's base case; key high-value launches back-ended (post FY28); India and ex-US/ex-India markets positive
Headwinds in the US to impact growth; Q1 was led by US exclusivities
Growth to take a hiatus: gTolvaptan, gMirabegron and gSpiriva are ~50% of EPS and face competition from Q2FY27/FY28; PAT to decline over FY26-28E
Muted FY27; launches across geographies drive FY28 growth and any re-rating
Downgraded from Buy (TP Rs2,540): US base losing momentum, little visibility on replacing gJynarque and gMyrbetriq; US ~USD975mn by FY29, margin ~20% by FY29
Ivacaftor (Kalydeco) patent win removes the main barrier to a first-to-file launch with 180-day exclusivity (USD20-30mn a year)

moat.soWhat: Real know-how few Indian peers have, but each product earns only until a rival is approved

moat.evidence: Tolvaptan (sole generic for 14+ months), Mirabegron (at-risk launch, then settled), ivacaftor win (Aug-2026); 50 FTFs incl. 21 exclusive
moat.soWhat: Produces windfalls, but they are lumpy and litigation-dependent

moat.evidence: No.8 in the IPM; 67% chronic; No.2 respiratory, No.3 cardiac and diabetes; Rx growing 1.1-1.3x the market; ~11,300 field force
moat.soWhat: Steady low-teens growth with high returns; the durable core

moat.evidence: Global leader in anti-TB and cephalosporin APIs; mostly captive; 15 plants
moat.soWhat: Helps margins and supply reliability; not a pricing moat

moat.evidence: VISUfarma ophthalmology footprint; biosimilars via partners; Brazil turnaround; No.4 in Australian generics
moat.soWhat: Growing 10-20% but subscale; margins improving from a low base

moat.evidence: Pegfilgrastim (launch H2FY27 via Valorum), Ranibizumab approved, apixaban oral suspension tentatively approved; ~USD50mn biosimilar sales today
Two open warning letters (Tarapur, Mandideep), Pithampur Unit-2 OAI; 2017 warning letter took six years to resolve
moat.soWhat: Inspection risk is a recurring cost of the US strategy

critiques: Three products (gTolvaptan, gMirabegron, gSpiriva) are ~50% of EPS and all face competition by FY28: earnings fall before launches replace them
The US base is losing momentum; US sales could fall to ~USD975mn by FY29 and margins to ~20%
Management's FY28 US growth guidance is not in the street's base case; the big launches are back-ended
The Mirabegron settlement adds a per-unit royalty and ~Rs420 cr a year of licence amortisation in FY27: the windfall is shrinking even before competition
Antitrust: DoJ investigation since 2017, state AG lawsuits; Rs582 cr provided in FY26 and more settlements likely
Bull view: apixaban oral suspension could be as large as Tolvaptan, ivacaftor adds an exclusivity, US back above USD300mn a quarter in FY28
Adjacencies (diagnostics, digital, OTC, CDMO) still lose money and cost 100-150bp of margin
gaps: Lupin does not disclose product-level US revenue; the share of Tolvaptan, Mirabegron and Spiriva comes only from brokers (PL: ~50% of EPS), so an ex-windfall EPS series or median cannot be built. We show a pre-windfall window (forward year FY24) instead.
